In this research, we use simulations to verify the propagating SAWs are able to bend the conduction band and valence band periodically on surface of semiconductor substrate. As a result, the electrons and holes in semiconductor material are spatially separated and transported by the SAWs.

articleTitle: Design and measurement of the KRISS Reverberation Chamber 1
publicationTitle: 2016 URSI Asia-Pacific Radio Science Conference (URSI AP-RASC)
abstract: A reverberation chamber (RC) had been used widely in the electromagnetic measurement area. An RC is designed to have a long reverberation time, generate a lot of mode, and good field uniformity within the chamber. The purpose of this paper is to describe the design process and measurement of the KRISS Reverberation Chamber 1 (KRC 1). KRC 1 with 4.5 m × 3.4 m × 2.8 m dimensions is simulated by FEKO software. Field uniformity then calculated at frequency 200 MHz, 252 MHz, 300 MHz, 357 MHz, and 400 MHz. Moreover, correlation coefficient is calculated at frequency 200 MHz, 300 MHz, and 400 MHz. The simulation result show good performance of the field uniformity and correlation coefficient and confirmed by measurement from frequency 200 MHz to 1 GHz.

articleTitle: Microwave sub-surface imaging using scattered-field calibration technique
publicationTitle: 2016 URSI Asia-Pacific Radio Science Conference (URSI AP-RASC)
abstract: A novel microwave sub-surface imaging scheme based on a scattered-field calibration technique is proposed in this paper. In this framework, the scattering parameters of the test object using the standard RF measurement system is first transformed into the electric field data. The transformation is based on measuring the scattering parameters of a known specimen under the same test environment, and then comparing the scattering parameters of this specimen with that of the test object under the assumption that electric field of the known specimen is computed in advance. The RF measurement system comprises of a transmitter-receiver array wherein the region under observation is illuminated sequentially. The solution of the inverse scattering problem is based on iterative distorted Born approximation. The performance of the proposed method is evaluated by means of numerical simulations and their inversion results.

articleTitle: Flooding area detection by ALOS-2 fully polarimetric data
publicationTitle: 2016 URSI Asia-Pacific Radio Science Conference (URSI AP-RASC)
abstract: This paper presents a detection result of flooding area in Joso-city, Japan, suffered from flood disaster caused by heavy rainfall on 2015 09 11. An emergency observation was carried out by the spaceborne sensor “ALOS-2” on 2015 09 16 using fully polarimetric data acquisition mode. Inundated areas were retrieved based on the magnitude of total power of the scene, and were validated with ground truth data. Good correspondence and scattering mechanism change from unflooded situation were identified by the fully polarimetric data.

articleTitle: Numerical analysis of electromagnetic band-stopping using non-metal periodic structures
publicationTitle: 2016 URSI Asia-Pacific Radio Science Conference (URSI AP-RASC)
abstract: We have analyzed the band-stopping characteristic of non-metal periodic structures for electromagnetic wave in a microwave region. The target frequencies are 2.4 and 5 GHz bands, which are popularly used in wireless LAN in Japan. There are two types of periodic structure in this article. One is the multilayer slab (a 1D photonic crystal) and the other is the square lattice of dielectric columns (a 2D photonic crystal). The finite-difference time-domain (FDTD) method is employed for the numerical calculation. Frequency and spatial characteristics of band-stopping are shown as numerical examples.

articleTitle: Development of 1.5 THz cartridge-type multi-pixel receiver based on HEB mixers
publicationTitle: 2016 URSI Asia-Pacific Radio Science Conference (URSI AP-RASC)
abstract: A novel design of 2 × 2 NbN hot electron bolometer (HEB) mixer array receiver has been demonstrated here by using the multiple local oscillator (LO) beams obtained from a power distributor. In our design, the 1.5 THz LO beam is split into four uniform sub-beams with a spacing of 18 mm, then arrives at a four-pixel silicon lens with twin slot antenna (TSA) through a large-area beam splitter. An additional four-pixel HDPE lens is located at 120 mm in front of the silicon lens to increase the size of beam waist for fitting to the aperture parameter of sub-reflector. This design can match the optical parameters between Si/TSA and GLT antenna. The pixel number can be further extended to 9 based on the available LO power.

articleTitle: Antenna pattern reconstruction of optical leaky waveguide antenna by phase-less measurement
publicationTitle: 2016 URSI Asia-Pacific Radio Science Conference (URSI AP-RASC)
abstract: This paper presents the antenna pattern reconstruction of optical leaky waveguides antenna by phase-less measurement. In recent years, there has been tremendous increased in data traffic due to the widespread of mobile terminals, and high data transmission system for next generation is expected. Optical communication is considered as one of those systems. We have studied grating (GWG) and waffle waveguides (WWG) which are a type of optical leaky waveguide antennas (OLWA). These antennas can tilt a beam by sweeping incident wavelength. Each waveguide measurement is evaluated at near field because the antenna structure is very large with respect to the wavelength. To evaluate the antenna pattern from near field of the beam scanning antenna, amplitude and phase are essential. In the experimental system of optical device, measuring intensity of the light is easy. The measurement of phase is difficult. In this study, directivity of each waveguide is estimated by the aperture distribution method using approximate aperture distribution. The proposed method shows that estimate gain and radiation angle are in good agreement with calculated result.

articleTitle: Performance analysis of LTE multi-antenna technology in live network
publicationTitle: 2016 URSI Asia-Pacific Radio Science Conference (URSI AP-RASC)
abstract: In this paper, we present several field trial results of LTE multi-antenna technology such as downlink 4×4 MIMO and uplink multi-user MIMO. At field trial, downlink 4×4 MIMO provides an average throughput increase of 42% compared to downlink 2×2 MIMO and uplink multi-user MIMO provides an average throughput increase of 33% compared to uplink 1×2 MIMO. In spite of these gains of LTE multi-antenna technologies, nearly all LTE base stations still use 2Tx and 2Rx antennas. Recently, LTE release 13 standard starts to support 16Tx base station, there is huge gap between standard and live network. By comparing the performance of LTE multi-antenna technologies with an alternative solution which has same network impacts, i.e., horizontal and vertical cell splitting, we provide what are the obstacles and which parts are needed to study further for commercialization of LTE multi-antenna technology.

articleTitle: Wearable and implantable magnetic resonant wireless power transfer
publicationTitle: 2016 URSI Asia-Pacific Radio Science Conference (URSI AP-RASC)
abstract: In this study, we suggested optimal design of in-body resonator by capacitance and air gap. We proposed magnetic resonance wireless power transfer (MR-WPT) system consisted of three resonators and was therefore called a three-resonator MR-WPT system. The proposed power transfer occurs between a wearable transmitter in the air and an implantable receiver in the fabricated muscle-mimicking liquid. According to the analysis of measurement results, the muscle-mimicking leads blocking on the H-field of MR-WPT system. This phenomenon has an affect the decreasing transfer efficiency that could be explained by the change in resonant frequency of the receiver resonator due to the impact of the dielectric constant and the conductivity of the MML liquid. To solve this problem, we suggested utilizing either an optimal capacitor or an air pocket to prevent the MML liquid from having this effect. These solutions improved the transfer efficiency of the MR-WPT system.

articleTitle: Design of all optical circular shift register using micro-ring resonator
publicationTitle: 2016 URSI Asia-Pacific Radio Science Conference (URSI AP-RASC)
abstract: The feasibility of implementing all-optical circular shift register is theoretically investigated and described using Silicon waveguide based micro-ring resonator (MRR) as nonlinear all-optical switch, which can be used as a building block for optical signal processing networks. The schemes of left and right circular shifting registers are proposed. The performance of the circuit is evaluated through numerical simulation, which confirms its feasibility in terms of the choice of the critical parameters.

articleTitle: Role of solar radio observations in Space Weather
publicationTitle: 2016 URSI Asia-Pacific Radio Science Conference (URSI AP-RASC)
abstract: The role of radio science in Space Weather ranges from use of radio techniques to measure plasma parameters at the Sun and in the heliosphere via remote-sensing, to direct impact of radio noise on wireless systems at Earth. This paper focuses on radio emission from the Sun, and summarizes the Space-Weather-relevant diagnostics available with a suite of new instruments capable of broadband radio imaging spectropolarimetry. We also discuss the potential for radio noise to directly interfere with Global Positioning System receivers, cellular telephone, and other wireless systems.

articleTitle: Millimeter-wave negative group delay network
publicationTitle: 2016 URSI Asia-Pacific Radio Science Conference (URSI AP-RASC)
abstract: This paper describes a negative differential-phase group delay network operating at millimeter-wave frequencies, which can be used to compensate for frequency variations in group delay that may otherwise cause signal distortion. This approach utilizes a defect waveguide with a high Q-factor defect cavity resonator, realized with a high-resistivity silicon-based 2D photonic crystal with engineered waveguide dispersion characteristics. We demonstrate a group delay of -151.8 ns at 99.74 GHz, with a correspondingly high figure of merit value of 3.34.

articleTitle: Microphysical characteristics analysis of three heavy snowfall events from the MASCRAD campaign in Greeley, Colorado, USA
publicationTitle: 2016 URSI Asia-Pacific Radio Science Conference (URSI AP-RASC)
abstract: Analysis of data from three snow events during the MASCRAD winter campaign in Greeley, Colorado, USA, are presented. The campaign entailed multi-angle snowflake camera (MASC), 2D-video disdrometer, precipitation occurrence sensor system, Pluvio gauge, weather station, all installed at the well-established MASCRAD (MASC + Radar) snow field site, as well as state-of-the-art S- and X-band polarimetric radars. We present here microphysical characteristics analysis for three heavy snowfall cases, on (a) 21–22 Feb 2015, (b) 15 Dec 2015, and (c) 01–02 Feb 2016.

articleTitle: Characteristics of GPS ionospheric scintillation and TEC depletion in the Chinese low latitude region
publicationTitle: 2016 URSI Asia-Pacific Radio Science Conference (URSI AP-RASC)
abstract: Using GPS ionospheric scintillation and TEC observations over low latitude stations in the Chinese sector, we investigated the occurrence characteristics of ionospheric scintillation and TEC depletions during 2004-2012. The results show that the GPS amplitude scintillation pattern, with a maximum during equinoctial months of solar maximum, agrees with plasma bubble and TEC depletion observations by in-situ satellites and ground based GPS receivers respectively. The scintillation onset during autumn months (September-October) is on average earlier than that of spring month (March-April) about 25 minutes. An analysis on the correlation of scintillation index S4 and TEC depletion index shows a good consistency during post-sunset hours. However, for the daytime periodic scintillation events detected during June solstice months of solar minimum, the simultaneous TEC observations show no significant depletion. On the other hand, by using spatially separated GPS scintillation/TEC receivers and VHF coherent scatter radar multiple beam steering observations over a low latitude station, Sanya (18.3°N, 109.6°E; dip lat. 12.8°N), we estimated the zonal drifts of irregularities producing strong scintillations. A similar behavior of zonal drifts, with slowly decreasing velocities at a rate of about 20 m/s/h, is found during the two equinoxes. Specifically, the zonal drifts of hundred meter and meter scale irregularities obtained from the two techniques respectively agree with each other.

articleTitle: Influence of induced voltage noise on switching characteristics for a power converter circuit
publicationTitle: 2016 URSI Asia-Pacific Radio Science Conference (URSI AP-RASC)
abstract: Recently, because of the development of power devices such as SiC and GaN devices, influence of parasitic parameters which are wiring inductance in power electronics circuits is discussed in many papers. However, it is should be discussed not only self-inductance but also mutual inductance in power electronics circuit. Because, power electronics circuits has some circuit loops such as main, gate-drive, and control circuits on one printed circuit board (PCB). This paper presents an influence of mutual inductance between main and gate-drive circuit, and simulation and experimental results, rated at 500 V and 20 A, will be shown.

articleTitle: Application of IPO method to calculate scattering by conducting and dielectric objects
publicationTitle: 2016 URSI Asia-Pacific Radio Science Conference (URSI AP-RASC)
abstract: To consider a large and complex conducting or dielectric structure, an iterative physical optics method is proposed. The scheme is numerically and experimentally verified for a scattering and radome problems.

articleTitle: Thermal empirical effect on the Kapton-based passive microstrip circuit
publicationTitle: 2016 URSI Asia-Pacific Radio Science Conference (URSI AP-RASC)
abstract: This paper proposes an empirical analysis of the thermal influence on the electrical behavior of a flexible passive patch antenna which is printed on a Kapton-based substrate. The measurement protocol along with the use of the thermal chamber enabling the temperature control is presented. The experimental setup for measuring the input reflection coefficient with temperature variation ranging from 25°C to 150°C is described. Then, the input impedance of the tested microstrip circuit is analyzed given the quality factor and the antenna bandwidth. It is seen that, increasing the temperature decreases the quality factor of the antenna which is also noticeable through the matching level of the reflection coefficient. This is mainly explained by the drop of the conductivity of the top conductor made by silver ink-jet printing.

articleTitle: Dispersion engineering of nonreciprocal metamaterials and their applications to leaky wave antennas
publicationTitle: 2016 URSI Asia-Pacific Radio Science Conference (URSI AP-RASC)
abstract: This paper reviews recent progress on dispersion engineering of nonreciprocal metamaterials and their applications to highly-efficient leaky wave antennas with the help of resonant system. They are implemented into beam-scanning antennas as well as circularly polarized antennas by using phase gradient of the fields along the resonators.

articleTitle: Frequency interference test-bed considering both interferer's frequency and time domain parameters
publicationTitle: 2016 URSI Asia-Pacific Radio Science Conference (URSI AP-RASC)
abstract: In this paper, we suggested a real-time frequency interference test-bed considering both interferer's frequency and time domain characteristics. Due to the versatile programming capability of universal software radio peripheral (USRP) and LabVIEW, actual frequency interference environments can be easily modeled. Therefore, performance degradation effects at a victim receiver due to actual multiple interferers, such as bit error rate (BER) and packet error rate (PER), can be analyzed intuitively. As an example, we demonstrated an interference scenario consisting of Zigbee node as a victim and Wi-Fi nodes as interferers. From the measured results, it was verified that our test-bed can model various real-time interference scenarios easily.

articleTitle: Resistive and distributed multiband NGD active circuit
publicationTitle: 2016 URSI Asia-Pacific Radio Science Conference (URSI AP-RASC)
abstract: A simple topology of negative group delay (NGD) distributed active circuit (NGDDAC) is analyzed in this paper. The NGD cell is composed of a field effect transistor (FET) associated with a series resistance in cascade with short-circuited stub line. The theoretical approach illustrating the determination of the proposed NGD circuit S-parameter modelling is presented. Then, the synthesis formulas enabling to determine the NGDDAC parameters in function of the expected NGD specifications are established. In difference with the lumped NGD circuits, the distributed proposed NGDDAC operates without need of lossy lumped inductance. To illustrate the NGD concept feasibility, a cell of NGDDAC integrating 16mm length microstrip stub using the pHEMT EC2612 is synthesized and simulated. It was found that the circuits generate 5GHz periodical multiband NGD with extremal peak of about -0.5ns over the bandwidth more than 1GHz.

articleTitle: Calibration of terahertz spectrum by using carbon monoxide
publicationTitle: 2016 URSI Asia-Pacific Radio Science Conference (URSI AP-RASC)
abstract: Terahertz time domain spectrometer is becoming an important tool for inspecting the molecular information located in terahertz region. In order to get reliable spectroscopy data, calibration of terahertz spectrum is discussed in this paper. We measured the terahertz absorption spectrum of carbon monoxide (CO) gas with our homemade spectrometer. Comparing the measured absorption frequencies with the corresponding standard data in JPL database, we got the error values, and their distribution law showed the values gave a linear correlation with the absorption frequency. Based on this correlation, an calibration model was established. We used the model to correct the experimental data, and the result showed the maximum error after correction was 8.6 GHz, which was an order lower than the error before correction. This states the model can be used to correct the error of the measured terahertz spectrum. At last, we draw a conclusion that the terahertz time domain spectrometer system is supposed to be calibrated, in this way, the terahertz spectrum of sample can obtain a high accuracy. The study contributes to the material identification and the construction of molecular spectroscopy database in terahertz region.

articleTitle: An 8×8 CPW MKIDs developed for terahertz superconducting imaging array
publicationTitle: 2016 URSI Asia-Pacific Radio Science Conference (URSI AP-RASC)
abstract: China is planning to construct a 5-meter THz telescope named DATE5 at Dome A, Antarctica. This paper reports on the development of an 8×8 CPW microwave kinetic detectors (MKIDs) for the terahertz superconducting imaging array (TeSIA), which is an instrument proposed for the DATE5. The 8×8 CPW MKIDs, operating at 0.35THz, make use of TiN superconducting film of Tc approximately equal to 4.3K. The resonance frequencies of the MKIDs span the 4-5.575GHz band with an interval of 25MHz. The design, fabrication and characterization of the 8×8 CPW MKIDs are presented.

articleTitle: Circularly polarized reconfigurable metaline antenna
publicationTitle: 2016 URSI Asia-Pacific Radio Science Conference (URSI AP-RASC)
abstract: A circularly polarized (CP) antenna is proposed, where four metalines are used as radiation elements. This CP antenna supports a negative phase constant current, leading to a small antenna height of approximately 1/100 wavelength. The same antenna characteristics are reproduced even when the feed point position is changed for beam-steering in the azimuth plane, because the metalines are arrayed symmetrically with respect to the antenna center point. Thus, this CP antenna works as a reconfigurable antenna. The radiation pattern and VSWR are analyzed and discussed.

articleTitle: Switched-beam wideband circularly polarized 2 × 2 antenna array
publicationTitle: 2016 URSI Asia-Pacific Radio Science Conference (URSI AP-RASC)
abstract: This paper presents a wideband circularly polarized (CP) beam-steering antenna with the capability of generating several steerable beams. A single radiator is first constructed with two triangular-shaped dipoles, and four parasitic elements for wide CP operation bandwidth. The array antenna is implemented in a 2 × 2 arrangement and fed by a four-input port feeding network for the beam steering operation. The proposed antenna can generate CP axial beams in several directions with a suitable feed excitation. The final design with an overall size of 2λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub> × 2λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub> × 0.2λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub> (at 6 GHz) showed that the proposed design exhibited approximately 48% and 46% impedance matching and axial ratio bandwidths, respectively. Furthermore, stable right-hand circular polarization radiation patterns with a gain of more than 11 dBic were observed for each beam direction.

articleTitle: A novel method to reduce physical dimensions of reflectarray antennas using near-field feeding
publicationTitle: 2016 URSI Asia-Pacific Radio Science Conference (URSI AP-RASC)
abstract: This work proposes a novel way to reduce overall volume of reflectarray antennas while maintaining aperture efficiency relatively high. Different from conventional approaches, a feeder antenna is placed very close to the proposed reflectarray ground plane. In order to prevent expected degradation in antenna performance, which is mainly because the feeder is very close to the reflectarray, we impose an additional condition maximizing constructive interference between direct and reflected waves. Consequently, we can show that our antenna can provide relative high antenna gain and aperture efficiency even the antenna is remarkably reduced. Excellent agreement between simulation and experiment proves the validity of our proposal.

articleTitle: Ka-band radiometric imaging using antennas with pattern synthesis
publicationTitle: 2016 URSI Asia-Pacific Radio Science Conference (URSI AP-RASC)
abstract: The paper is devoted to experimental investigation of coherent radiometric imaging in azimuth-range plane. The Ka-band radar system suggested is a version of bistatic noise waveform SAR (Synthetic Aperture Radar) using two antennas with pattern synthesis and additional receive channel used as a reference signal. Indoor radiometric imaging has been validated using absorbers as the targets. These experiments enabled to estimate both range and angular resolution capabilities of a new radiometric system that was achieved due to application antennas with pattern synthesis and SAR signal processing. This estimate may be done within the range span limited by bistatic radiometer baseline.

articleTitle: Connector conversion technique for general-purpose connectors in S-parameter calibration
publicationTitle: 2016 URSI Asia-Pacific Radio Science Conference (URSI AP-RASC)
abstract: This paper proposes the connector conversion technique for a calibration of scattering parameter (S-parameter) calibration. The connector conversion adapter is characterized in dimensional measurement. It was confirmed the reasonable result from 9 kHz to 1000 MHz by phase measurement. We establish measurement of the F75 general-purpose connector from the connector conversion technique.

articleTitle: A 20 year decline in solar magnetic fields and solar wind micro-turbulence levels: Are we heading towards a Maunder-like minimum?
publicationTitle: 2016 URSI Asia-Pacific Radio Science Conference (URSI AP-RASC)
abstract: Our study of solar high-latitude (≥45°) photospheric magnetic fields and interplanetary scintillation observations, at 327 MHz, of solar wind micro-turbulence levels showed a steady decline for the past 20 years. Also, the fact that cycle 24 has already past its peak, implies that high-latitude fields are likely to decline until ~2020. Based on a correlation between the solar high-latitude fields and the heliospheric magnetic fields (HMF), we estimated the HMF strength in 2020 and the floor value of the HMF, which were found to be 3.9 (±0.6) nT and 3.2 (±0.4) nT, respectively. Using estimated value of the HMF in 2020, the peak sunspot number for solar Cycle 25 was estimated to be 62 (±12). These results and the fact that solar magnetic fields continues to decline at present raise the question of a very low sunspot activity in near-future or another grand minimum similar to the Maunder minimum. So what is the possible impact of such a likely grand minimum on terrestrial ionospheric current systems? Our study night time F-region maximum electron density (a measure of terrestrial ionospheric currents) reveals that the impending minimum is not likely to have any adverse impact rather the period post cycle 25 will be useful for undertaking systematic ground based low-frequency radio astronomy as the night time ionospheric cutoff-frequency could be well below 10 MHz.

articleTitle: Shape identification of perfectly conducting, arc-like crack in Transverse Electric mode
publicationTitle: 2016 URSI Asia-Pacific Radio Science Conference (URSI AP-RASC)
abstract: We investigate mathematical representation between subspace migration imaging function and Bessel function for a fast shape identification of perfectly conducting, arc-like crack in two-dimensional homogeneous space. This is based on the factorization of so-called Multi-Static Response (MSR) matrix, whose elements are measured far-field pattern in Transverse Electric (TE) mode. Identified representation will enables us to examine various undiscovered properties of imaging function. Numerical results via noisy data has been performed for supporting our investigations.

articleTitle: Suppression of multi-path coupling in scaled-down experiment using cross-borehole pulse radar
publicationTitle: 2016 URSI Asia-Pacific Radio Science Conference (URSI AP-RASC)
abstract: A scaled-down experiment using cross-borehole pulse radar is performed in laboratory to extract a more precise decision rule on detecting an intrusive man-made tunnel in Korea. To minimize the total size, a scaled-down model of an air-filled tunnel in underground rock is replaced by a cylindrical ceramic rod in pure water. When the upper arm of sleeve dipole antenna of the scaled-down cross-borehole pulse radar is directly connected to coaxial cable, the measured B-scan data are contaminated by unwanted striped pattern. Such multi-path coupling between the sleeve antenna pair is generated by the glass tube-guided waves. To suppress the glass tube-guided waves, the coaxial cable is clad in ferrite cores. As the total length of the ferrite core loading is increased up to 150 mm, the unwanted coupling is suppressed gradually and the target signature can be recognized more clearly.

articleTitle: Interpretation method for response waveform of transient scattered magnetic field by a coated cylinder covered with a thick material
publicationTitle: 2016 URSI Asia-Pacific Radio Science Conference (URSI AP-RASC)
abstract: We briefly propose an interpretation method for a response waveform of a transient scattered magnetic field by a two-dimensional coated cylinder by using a novel time-domain (TD) asymptotic-numerical solution (TD-ANS). We assume that the thickness of a coating medium is thick as compared with the wavelength of a central angular frequency of a high-frequency (HF) pulse wave radiated from a magnetic line source. Multiple reflected waves passing through a coating medium are added to the novel TD-ANS as compared with a conventional TD-ANS. The TD-ANS can extract each pulse wave element from a response waveform. The validity of an interpretation method for a response waveform is confirmed by comparing with a reference solution.

articleTitle: Design of a periodic structure to improve isolation using ferrite material for small CRPA arrays
publicationTitle: 2016 URSI Asia-Pacific Radio Science Conference (URSI AP-RASC)
abstract: This paper proposes a periodic structure to improve isolation using ferrite materials for small controlled reception pattern antenna arrays. The periodic structure is composed of metal and ferrite plates with high permeability, and the ferrite material is used as a replacement of the perfect magnetic conductor in the soft surface to reduce the size of the corrugated geometry. This structure improves the isolation between array elements by eliminating the tangential components of electric and magnetic fields on the surface of metal and ferrite plates, respectively. The result shows that the proposed structure is capable of improving the isolation in extremely small arrays.

articleTitle: Research of quality of nonlinear Markov filtering RGB signal in conditions of Gaussian and non-Gaussian noise
publicationTitle: 2016 URSI Asia-Pacific Radio Science Conference (URSI AP-RASC)
abstract: A quasi-optimal receiving algorithm for the RGB signals based on the Markov theory of nonlinear filtering is designed. Evaluating the synthesized algorithm effectiveness is founded on the image processing digital simulation of the signal mixed with the Johnson and white Gaussian noises. Examples of filter operation with different value of signal to noise ratio are presented. A comparative analysis is performed and the kind of noise for the best filtering is defined. It is shown the developed algorithm allows one to filter RGB signal better than the adaptive algorithm for the same a priori information about the signal.

articleTitle: Volume singular integro-differential equations in the electromagnetic diffraction problem
publicationTitle: 2016 URSI Asia-Pacific Radio Science Conference (URSI AP-RASC)
abstract: The problem of diffraction of electromagnetic waves on a 3-dimensional inhomogeneous dielectric body in a free space is considered. The original boundary value problem is reduced to a volume singular integro-differential equation. It is proved that for smooth data the solution from L<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> will necessary be continuous down to the boundary of the body. The equivalency between the boundary value problem and the integro-differential equation is proved. In addition, using pseudodifferential operators calculus, ellipticity of the operator of the problem is proved.

articleTitle: A co-polarization ratio-based parameter for urban man-made target detection
publicationTitle: 2016 URSI Asia-Pacific Radio Science Conference (URSI AP-RASC)
abstract: Backscatter from man-made buildings in urban areas in polarimetric synthetic aperture radar (SAR) images is generally characterized by strong backscattered energy, the double-bounce scattering property, the polarization orientation angle, and scattering helicity. Polarimetric parameters that represent either double-bounce or helix scattering properties are usually used as indicators for man-made target identification. For the first time, a co-polarization ratio-based parameter is used to characterize the scattering from man-made structures, which usually exhibit both reflection symmetry and asymmetry. The parameter was firstly derived from a symmetric scattering model, and in this study we analyze this parameter under the refection asymmetric case, where the target helicity angle is taken into consideration. Experiments demonstrated on RADARSAT-2 multi-temporal polarimetric data show the effectiveness of this parameter in distinguishing urban areas from other land cover types.

articleTitle: 8192 Mbps wideband correlation for the KaVA
publicationTitle: 2016 URSI Asia-Pacific Radio Science Conference (URSI AP-RASC)
abstract: Daejeon hardware correlator is designed and implemented with performance of maximum 16 stations, 8192 Mbps, and 8192 channels output. However, VLBI observation is generally conducted with 1024 Mbps recording speed and the recording speed for wideband as like 2048 and 8192 Mbps are experimentally tested and increasingly conducted. In this paper, we introduce the required system so as to carry out the 8192 Mbps wideband correlation for maximum performance of Daejeon hardware correlator. Especially the data splitting and data transmission, data playback to correlator, and correlation processing method will be briefly introduced.

articleTitle: Systematic shifts in the frequency of NPLI-CsF1
publicationTitle: 2016 URSI Asia-Pacific Radio Science Conference (URSI AP-RASC)
abstract: At CSIR-National Physical Laboratory, India (NPLI) we have developed first generation of Cesium atomic fountain (NPLI-CsF1) primary frequency standard (PFS). NPLI-CsF1 is now fully operational and its frequency is now being evaluated along with all systematic and statistical uncertainties. The present experimental data conforms that fountain frequency is stable to few parts in 1015 at less than one day averaging time. The fountain frequency is compared with the Hydrogen MASER (H-MASER) which is contributing to TAI already and hence fountain frequency is traceable to TAI. Recent evaluation results were communicated to BIPM and published in circular T. Typical stability of NPLI CsF1 is ∼7 × 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−13</sup> τ<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−1/2</sup>. The present performance of fountain is limited by the measurement uncertainty of cold collisional shift.

articleTitle: Scattering by a metallic wedge cylindrically capped with penetrable materials
publicationTitle: 2016 URSI Asia-Pacific Radio Science Conference (URSI AP-RASC)
abstract: A metallic wedge cylindrically coated by two coaxial penetrable materials is considered. The inner cylinder coating the edge is made of either a DPS material or a DNG metamaterial, and is in turn coated by a layer of DPS material. The primary field is a plane wave incident normally to the edge of the wedge. An exact analytical solution is obtained, and numerical results are presented and discussed.

articleTitle: Tolerance analysis of antenna array pattern in the presence of array weights and element position errors
publicationTitle: 2016 URSI Asia-Pacific Radio Science Conference (URSI AP-RASC)
abstract: This paper analyzes pattern tolerance against errors of excitation amplitude and element position in uniform linear arrays. The upper and lower bounds of the array pattern are derived based on the interval arithmetic. Compared to existing bounds, the proposed bounds consider both amplitude and position errors, and they are useful to understand the pattern tolerance when both amplitude and position errors exist in real arrays. Computer simulations are conducted to validate the effectiveness of the derived bounds.

articleTitle: Prediction of convective rainfall using multi-technique observations
publicationTitle: 2016 URSI Asia-Pacific Radio Science Conference (URSI AP-RASC)
abstract: Nowcasting of rain amount is extremely essential in various fields of life. In this paper, we have shown that monitoring of brightness temperature at 31.4 GHz, the frequency having strong absorption due to liquid water, can give an estimate of rain accumulation with a prediction efficiency of ~ 80 % and a lead time of 75 minutes. It has also been observed that atmospheric electric field also shows definite changes before rain the magnitude of which can be related with the rainfall amount.

articleTitle: Numerical modeling of thick conducting irises using FDTD method-comparison with the modified residue-calculus method
publicationTitle: 2016 URSI Asia-Pacific Radio Science Conference (URSI AP-RASC)
abstract: In this paper, we investigate the accuracy of the finite-difference time-domain (FDTD) method for approximating a waveguide consisting of a periodic structure with a conducting iris of nonzero thickness. We consider a model for a single stage of a periodic structure - an individual conducting iris of nonzero thickness - and determine optimal grid spacings for FDTD calculations. We determine the optimal grid spacings using benchmark numerical solutions obtained with the modified residue-calculus method (MRCM), an accurate solution procedure that incorporates boundary conditions. We obtain agreement by choosing a grid spacing on the order of 1/100th of the wavelength λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">g</sub>.

articleTitle: Composites with radially anisotropic cylinders
publicationTitle: 2016 URSI Asia-Pacific Radio Science Conference (URSI AP-RASC)
abstract: This presentation contains a brief review of the electrostatic polarizability of RA circular cylinders and the quasi-dynamic homogenization of such cylinders in a square lattice. The previous results are verified using new full-wave computations modeling the square lattice of RA cylinders as a photonic crystal. In all cases the electric field is assumed to be perpendicular to the cylinder axis (TE polarization).

articleTitle: EM fields in the model of biological cell
publicationTitle: 2016 URSI Asia-Pacific Radio Science Conference (URSI AP-RASC)
abstract: Mobile phone communication infrastructure has promoted possible health effects of radio frequency electromagnetic energy, emanating from mobile phone antenna. In every day, people are affected by the radiation of electromagnetic field emitted from mobile phone antenna. The effect of the radiation directly cannot calculated because of the complexity of the human body structure. One major factor is considered among many other factor is the skin depth (SD). In this study, we evaluate the numerical analysis of the skin depth with respect to the frequency of mobile phone. A model is developed and, results from the model was analysis and also compare result theoretically with the literature and good agreements are obtained.

articleTitle: Specific absorption rates in human brain for different length of bar phones
publicationTitle: 2016 URSI Asia-Pacific Radio Science Conference (URSI AP-RASC)
abstract: A specific anthropomorphic mannequin (SAM) phantom is a standard head model for assessing the specific absorption rate (SAR) compliance of mobile phones. Most bar-type phones commercially released in Korea have the internal antenna at the bottom of the phone body. The phone length and the spatial peak 1-g SAR of commercial phones were investigated. The spatial peak SAR values in the SAM phantom and human brains for simple bar-type phone models with different body length are numerically analyzed. The SAR change rates according to phone lengths are compared between in the human brains and in the SAM phantom are different.

articleTitle: Hysteresis and jump phenomena in Reflex Oscillators
publicationTitle: 2016 URSI Asia-Pacific Radio Science Conference (URSI AP-RASC)
abstract: This paper aims at developing the analysis for the observation of hysteresis and jump phenomena in Reflex Klystron Oscillators (RKO) in the presence of synchronizing signal. The analysis takes into account the quadrature component of electron beam current apart from the in phase component, the quadrature phase component being responsible for producing asymmetry in the frequency response of the oscillator. This effect is not observed when the quadrature component is ignored like most previous authors. Power versus steady state amplitude characteristics has been explored along with the stability boundaries.

articleTitle: Electrical characteristics of and E-field distribution in CTL (Coupled-transmission-line) cell for SAR measurement probe calibration at 150 MHz
publicationTitle: 2016 URSI Asia-Pacific Radio Science Conference (URSI AP-RASC)
abstract: Many countries are regulating rf absorption of mobile terminals because of possible hazardous effect by wireless handsets. S. Korean government made public for the first time in the world that 150 MHz portable radio transceiver shall be regulated by SAR. So it needs to develop calibration system of SAR measurement for 150 MHz band. It includes to produce semi-uniform E-field and H-field in an appropriate volume to calibrate the SAR measurement probe. CTL cell was developed for this purpose and tested to check its validity to calibrate the probe. E-fields in air and in the human simulating liquid in the developed CTL cell were measured. It was verified that uniform field in the cell was excited in air. Although E-field distribution in the simulant liquid was nonuniform by the long distance, but the cell gives uniform enough space for calibrating a SAR measurement probe in the short distance.

articleTitle: A linear HBT power amplifier with an IMD3 reduction method for LTE-A small-cell base-station applications
publicationTitle: 2016 URSI Asia-Pacific Radio Science Conference (URSI AP-RASC)
abstract: A highly linear HBT power amplifier (PA) for LTE-A small-cell base-stations is presented. By separating a bias point of the PA sub-cells and combining these outputs with out-of phasing, the third-order intermodulation distortion (IMD) can be reduced. By the simulation results, the third-order IMDs are approximately -50 dBc and -43 dBc with and without the separate biasing at an output power of 29 dBm, respectively. The designed HBT PA has a gain of 31 dB, a P1dB of 35 dBm, and a PAE of 38.1% under 5 V supply voltage.

articleTitle: Incompletely modulated PSK signal reception using modified balanced optical phase-locked loop
publicationTitle: 2016 URSI Asia-Pacific Radio Science Conference (URSI AP-RASC)
abstract: A homodyne optical communication system using incomplete phase modulated PSK signal is considered. The phase-error variance of the system critically depends on the phase deviation parameter between the two transmitted bits. Also, optical phase-locked loop (OPLL) has finite loop-delay. All these venomous effects put constraints on the performance of a conventional OPLL based PSK receiver. A modified balanced OPLL based homodyne PSK signal reception system overcome some of these limitations, offers a much improved tracking performance and also provides more relaxed line-width requirement, improved tolerance and performance against delay.

articleTitle: Rigorous calculation of scattered field by conductive disk using multiple precision arithmetic -calculation precision and parameter selection
publicationTitle: 2016 URSI Asia-Pacific Radio Science Conference (URSI AP-RASC)
abstract: The electromagnetic scattering caused by a circular disk of perfect conductor has been analyzed rigorously and numerical data for scattered fields have been reported for circular disks having radii smaller than 3.0 wavelengths. By introducing multiple precision arithmetic, numerical data are obtained for disks of larger radii. However, multiple precision arithmetic consumes a lot of calculation time. In addition, a number of matrix equations of the large matrix size must be calculated. In this paper, we investigate optimal data lengths, optimal matrix size and the optimal number of matrix equations. As a result, the optimal data lengths, the optimal number of matrix equations and the optimal matrix size linearly increases as the radius of the disk increases.

articleTitle: Acoustic planar magnifying hyperlens
publicationTitle: 2016 URSI Asia-Pacific Radio Science Conference (URSI AP-RASC)
abstract: In this work, we propose an acoustic planar magnifying hyperlens. The lens consists of the parallel-arranged channels with periodically varied cross-sections. The overall hyperbolic dispersion behavior makes the lens capable of converting near-field evanescent waves to fat-field propagating waves. Simulation results verify the super-resolution magnifying imaging of the proposed hyperlens.

articleTitle: The suitability of cloud, massive and moderate computing environments for SKA scale data
publicationTitle: 2016 URSI Asia-Pacific Radio Science Conference (URSI AP-RASC)
abstract: We present the results of our investigations into options for the computing platform for the imaging pipeline in the CHILES project, an ultra-deep HI pathfinder for the era of the Square Kilometre Array. CHILES pushes the current computing infrastructure to its limits and understanding how to deliver the images from this project is clarifying the Science Data Processing requirements for the SKA. We have tested three platforms: a moderately sized cluster, a massive High Performance Computing (HPC) system, and the Amazon Web Services (AWS) cloud computing platform. We are able to complete the imaging pipeline processing on both the HPC platform and also on the cloud computing platform, which paves the way for meeting big data challenges in the era of SKA in the field of Radio Astronomy.

articleTitle: Avoidance of off-switch resonance in true time delay line using cascaded switches
publicationTitle: 2016 URSI Asia-Pacific Radio Science Conference (URSI AP-RASC)
abstract: In this paper, we propose the design of switched line True time delay (TTD) using cascaded switches, which removes off-switch resonance. Conventional switched lines with two different delay-time difference, 15ps and 270p, are presented to indicate that off-switch resonances can be observed in switched lines using switches with a fair isolation of 15dB. Switched line with cascaded switches is designed and fabricated to show the resonance can be eliminated. All designs are conducted in consideration of matching. The measured results are in agreement with the simulation results in CST Design Studio.

articleTitle: Irregularity observation with multiple VHF coherent radars in China
publicationTitle: 2016 URSI Asia-Pacific Radio Science Conference (URSI AP-RASC)
abstract: VHF coherent radar has been widely used in the investigation of ionospheric irregularity over the past three decades. To get a better understanding of the occurrence characteristic of ionospheric irregularity and the mechanism behind it over the low latitude region of China, a VHF radar has been operated at Sanya since 2009. In this paper, we present a brief review of irregularity observations, including ionospheric E, valley and F region irregularities, and meteor trail irregularity with the Sanya VHF radar. Specifically, two more VHF radars (newly installed at Wuhan and Qujing respectively) began operation recently to observe ionospheric irregularity over middle latitude in China. Preliminary results from a simultaneous observation by the three VHF radars are also presented.

articleTitle: Sparsity reconstruction algorithm for nonlinear microwave problems
publicationTitle: 2016 URSI Asia-Pacific Radio Science Conference (URSI AP-RASC)
abstract: This paper analyzes a recent sparse reconstruction algorithm applied to the nonlinear inverse scattering problem arising in microwave imaging to determine the dielectric contrast from measured fields. The sparsity of contrast profile with respect to a certain base is a priori assumed. The proposed iterative algorithm of soft shrinkage type enforces the sparsity constraint at each nonlinear iteration. The scheme produces sharp and good reconstruction of dielectric profiles in sparse domains by adapting Barzilai and Borwein (BB) step size selection criteria and projection constraint on contrast by maintaining its convergence during the reconstruction. Numerical results show the effectiveness and accuracy of the proposed method by considering randomly measured fields and emphasizing the sensitivity of the choice of regularization parameter.

articleTitle: Gravity loading effect analysis of the 5 meter Terahertz antenna for Dome A, Antarctica
publicationTitle: 2016 URSI Asia-Pacific Radio Science Conference (URSI AP-RASC)
abstract: The terahertz windows of 5 meter Dome A Terahertz Explorer (DATE5) are primarily over the wavelengths between 350 and 200 μm. For studying the performance of the DATE5, based on a finite element model of the whole telescope assembly, the deformations of the telescope under gravity load at different pointing are calculated. The obtained results show the ranges of surface RMS errors is in [2.59 μm, 4.11μm]. All of the surface RMS errors are smaller than 5.00μm, which meet the performance requirements for the telescope. Besides, the results show that surface RMS errors due to gravity loading increase as the elevation angle increase. There is a nonlinear dependence of the reflector surface RMS error over the elevation angles. It can be fitted to a sine function.

articleTitle: Computational estimation of the induced electric fields in visual tissues by circular-Halo coil
publicationTitle: 2016 URSI Asia-Pacific Radio Science Conference (URSI AP-RASC)
abstract: The Halo-circular assembly coil (HCA coil) shows the promise for direct stimulation of deeper brain tissues noninvasively. It provides significant advantages over alternative invasive methods of stimulating neurons at depth in the brain. This paper focused on investigating the induced electric fields in eyeball tissues and optical nerve by using the HCA coil. Three-dimensional distributions of the induced electric field in realistic head model were obtained by impedance method, and the results were compared with the normal circular coil. It was observed the induced electric field in optical nerve is always higher than that in eyeball tissues for both HCA and normal circular coils. Numerical results suggest the potential risk in the excitation of visual nerves in using HCA coil in deep transcranial magnetic stimulation (dTMS).

articleTitle: Position-freshness based intermediate node filtering for VANET
publicationTitle: 2016 URSI Asia-Pacific Radio Science Conference (URSI AP-RASC)
abstract: Inter-vehicle communication has challenges caused by characteristics of vehicle. High mobility of the vehicle induce change of network topology. Many routing protocols has been proposed to address high mobility. Among them, position based routing (PBR) protocols are getting attentions as a suited method. In PBR, forwarding node select intermediate nodes based on neighbor node's position information. Since PBR can reduce end-to-end delay by transmit packets without route establish, getting attentions as a suitable routing protocol for inter-vehicle communication. However, inaccuracies of the position information and disturbance of transmission by obstacles decreases the reliability of the packet delivery. In this paper, we propose filtering method of candidate nodes based on position information freshness. By filtering untrusted nodes, proposed method can improve reliability of transmission in urban environment.

articleTitle: Measurement of ionosphere over the western pacific ocean
publicationTitle: 2016 URSI Asia-Pacific Radio Science Conference (URSI AP-RASC)
abstract: It is increasing to measure the ionosphere over the ocean, since it occupies 70% of whole ionosphere and it is necessary for improving the precision of empirical/numerical models. Especially, as the operational aviation requires the precise ionospheric information, it is indispensable to develop the methods of measurement of ionosphere over the ocean. This paper discuss some method and introduce some project which already starts.

articleTitle: Transmission and resonance of a single rectangular hole filled with anisotropic material
publicationTitle: 2016 URSI Asia-Pacific Radio Science Conference (URSI AP-RASC)
abstract: This work presents, for the first time, a general theoretical framework of the transmission and resonance of a single rectangular hole filled with uniaxial anisotropic material. It has been shown that compared to the case that the aperture is filled with the isotropic material, the richer remarkably resonances can be obtained by using the aperture filled with the anisotropic material. More importantly, we demonstrate that the desired resonance behavior can be achieved by the dielectric and permeability tensors of filling material, besides the size of aperture, in a flexible way. Three special cases-positive, negative and extreme anisotropy, are studied to verify the proposed methodology.

articleTitle: Multiphysics modeling and simulation of plasma sheath
publicationTitle: 2016 URSI Asia-Pacific Radio Science Conference (URSI AP-RASC)
abstract: The interaction problems between EM-wave and plasma sheath should be solved by applying the magneto-hydrodynamics (MHD) equations which are coupled by fluid mechanics equations and electrodynamics equations. However, it is very difficult to solve the MHD equations directly by numerical simulation technique. A multiphysics modeling of plasma sheath is set up in this paper to simplify the interaction mechanism between EM-wave and plasma sheath. The hypersonic flow field of themochemical nonequilibrium is simulated and the variations on pressure, temperature and electron density are presented. Thus, EM parameters such as dielectric constant and permeability can be derived and used for EM simulation.

articleTitle: Kalman tracking of mobile devices considering range-free localization accuracy
publicationTitle: 2016 URSI Asia-Pacific Radio Science Conference (URSI AP-RASC)
abstract: The estimated position of range-free localization is sensitive to change of connectivity information between mobile devices. To compensate the defect, we propose a Kalman tracking of mobile devices with range-free localization. We analyze the performance results with aspects of range-free localization accuracy and real indoor environment.

articleTitle: Wide-angle generalization of integral representation as double weighted Fourier transform in the problem of wave reflection from a randomly inhomogeneous ionospheric layer
publicationTitle: 2016 URSI Asia-Pacific Radio Science Conference (URSI AP-RASC)
abstract: It has been shown before that the method of double weighted Fourier transform (DWFT) allows us to describe in a small-angle approximation Fresnel and caustic diffraction effects, as well as multipath propagation effects that occur in radio wave propagation through multi-scale inhomogeneous ionospheric plasma. For wide-angle generalization of this approach, in this report we employ the Fock proper-time method. The solution obtained, along with the above properties of the small-angle variant of DWFT, describes wave reflection from a randomly inhomogeneous layer and specifies conditions under which the spatial signal processing based on the inverse DWFT can increase resolution of vertical ionospheric sounding.

articleTitle: Quantitative assessment of earth's radiation belt electron acceleration
publicationTitle: 2016 URSI Asia-Pacific Radio Science Conference (URSI AP-RASC)
abstract: The highly dynamical evolution of the Earth's Van Allen radiation belt electron fluxes is due to competitions between various loss and acceleration processes. In this paper, we focus on analyzing an interesting event, where electrons experienced very rapid acceleration from hundreds of keV to multi-MeV within 12-16 hours in the heart of the outer radiation belt. Using 3D particle diffusion code, we simulate radiation belt electron evolution by including important physical processes, such as radial diffusion due to interaction with ultra-low-frequency waves, as well as pitch angle and energy diffusion driven by whistler-mode chorus waves. A quantitative comparison against the Van Allen Probes electron measurements clearly shows that chorus waves play a critical role in accelerating electrons to multiple MeV through producing the growing peaks in electron phase space density and the characteristic flat-top pitch angle distributions, while radial diffusion plays an important role in redistributing electrons from the developing peaks to other locations.

articleTitle: Nonlinear dynamics of electrons interacting with oblique whistler mode waves in the magnetosphere
publicationTitle: 2016 URSI Asia-Pacific Radio Science Conference (URSI AP-RASC)
abstract: We investigate the properties of whistler-mode wave particle interactions at oblique angles to the background magnetic field. We compare an exact formula of oblique whistler-mode dispersion relation with that of the quasi-longitudinal approximation. We derive a group velocity of an oblique whistler-mode wave as a function of wave frequency, wave vector, and wave normal angle. We find that the angle between the group velocity and the background magnetic field is always less than 30° even if the wave normal angle is up to 80° for the wave frequency less than 0.5 times the electron gyrofrequency. This relation points out that the wave energy is always transported parallel to the ambient magnetic field. Landau resonance, which appear in oblique whistler-mode waves but not in parallel waves, results in significant electron acceleration. To reveal the physical process and the efficiency of electron acceleration, we perform test particle simulations with electrons started at specific equatorial pitch angles and kinetic energies. By confirming that the group velocity is nearly parallel to the background magnetic field, we utilize gyro-averaging method, which averages the cyclotron motion at gyro-center and reduces the simulation from two-dimensional system to one-dimensional system. The simulation results show that 10-1000keV electrons can be accelerated to multi-MeV energy through Landau resonance as well as the cyclotron resonance.

articleTitle: Development of the exposure apparatus of intermediate frequency magnetic field for mice and biological effects on blood properties
publicationTitle: 2016 URSI Asia-Pacific Radio Science Conference (URSI AP-RASC)
abstract: To explore the possible non-thermal biological effects of the intermediate frequency magnetic field, we have developed the exposure apparatus for 85 kHz time varying magnetic field. When the current of 30Arms is applied to the solenoidal coil, effective value of alternating magnetic flux density 6.5 mT is obtained. It is found that, induced electric field of 7.8V/m, that is whole body average, will be achieved by this exposure system. As preliminary experiment, we exposed this magnetic field to mice for 1 hour and examined the effect on blood properties.

articleTitle: Sub-terahertz slow-wave circuits for coherent radiation sources
publicationTitle: 2016 URSI Asia-Pacific Radio Science Conference (URSI AP-RASC)
abstract: In this letter, we propose sub-terahertz (sub-THz) slow-wave circuits for coherent radiation sources through beam-wave interaction mechanism. The circuits are prepared using microfabrication in advanced silicon (Si) technologies. Our approach is to split the circuit into multi levels allowing a low aspect ratio configuration and alleviating the loading effect of deep-reactive-ion etching on silicon wafers. This makes it easier to achieve flat-etched bottom and smooth sidewall profiles in nanoscale accuracy for high frequency operation. The dispersion relation retrieved from the measurement, therefore, corresponds well to the theoretical estimation. In particular, the sub-THz radiation is successfully measured in pulsed operation through the vacuum-sealed integration of the slow-wave circuit with a 15-kV, 90-mA thermionic electron gun. This observation offers a promising opportunity for the development of terahertz radiation sources based on silicon micro- and nanofabrication technologies.

articleTitle: Closed-form expression of axial ratio for circularly polarized patch antenna with perturbation segments
publicationTitle: 2016 URSI Asia-Pacific Radio Science Conference (URSI AP-RASC)
abstract: We present a simple and accurate closed-form expression to compute the axial ratio of a single feed patch antenna with perturbation segments. The closed-form expression is derived from the antenna input impedance obtained from an equivalent circuit representing the resonant behaviors of two degenerated modes in the antenna. Using this equation, the axial ratio can be predicted by the input impedance, which can be simply measured using a network analyzer instead of measuring the fields in an antenna chamber. We checked the validity of derived equation by comparing to full-wave simulation data of a GPS L1 band antenna. The results show that a good agreement with an error less than 0.13% and 0.3% in the prediction of center frequency and bandwidth of axial ratio.

articleTitle: A novel method for the design of broadband class E power amplifier with contiguous diplexer
publicationTitle: 2016 URSI Asia-Pacific Radio Science Conference (URSI AP-RASC)
abstract: This work concentrates on the design of high efficient class E at octave bandwidths which is a challenge, nowadays, in design broadband class E. To solve this problem, a novel topology of class E amplifier is proposed by using contiguous diplexers. Firstly, the diplexer subdivides the operating wide bands into operating sub-bands. When operating in narrow band, the class E amplifier easily has much better match over its operating band and therefore provide better efficiency. Secondly, after amplifying the sub-band signals, the diplexer re-combines them into one band as the original. A validated simulation obtaining an average PAE of 78% is implemented at an octave band of 1 GHz to 2 GHz with a output power of 10 W.

articleTitle: Research on calibration technology of the wide spectrum grating monochromator wavelength accuracy
publicationTitle: 2016 URSI Asia-Pacific Radio Science Conference (URSI AP-RASC)
abstract: The wide spectrum of grating monochromator output wavelength accuracy is one of the main parameters of the monochromator, At present the calibration of monochromator output wavelength of most of the mercury lamp, to complete the calibration of the monochromator output wavelength in the visible range, but is unable to satisfy the calibration in the infrared wavelength. Aiming at the need for calibration, and based on the principle of grating diffraction, puts forword a method of using laser diffuse reflection method for measuring the wide spectrum of grating monochromator output wavelength accuracy. Select 632.8nm, 1550nm, 3.39µm three laser as the light source for calibration of grating monochromator, each laser measurement of three order diffraction. And the extension of the method of measurement uncertainty was evaluated and analysis, expanded measurement uncertainty of the method was 0.5%. Finally selects grating monochromator, the expanded uncertainty of measurement is verified, show that the measurement method is feasible, can meet the demand of high precision grating monochromator calibration.

articleTitle: Study on the gain-flatness characteristics of backward-pumped distributed fiber Raman amplifier based on the genetic algorithm
publicationTitle: 2016 URSI Asia-Pacific Radio Science Conference (URSI AP-RASC)
abstract: A theoretical model based on the genetic algorithm is proposed and presented to analyze the gain flatness-characteristics of backward-pumped distributed fiber Raman amplifier (B-DFRA). The relationship between the gain flatness performances with the pump wavelength spacing in B-DFRA is demonstrated theoretically. It is shown that the minimum gain ripple of the B-DFRA can be obtained by optimizing the power of pump source using the genetic algorithm, and the gain spectrum of the B-DFRA which pump wavelengths are arranged in a geometric proportion interval sequence is flatter than the one which pump wavelengths are arranged in an equal interval sequence in the same conditions. Moreover, a design example of an 80-nm bandwidth B-DFRA with the gain ripple of 0.48 dB is presented to verify the accuracy of the theoretical model. This research provides a useful guide to the fabrication of practical B-DFRA.

articleTitle: Challenges of space borne radio diagnostics
publicationTitle: 2016 URSI Asia-Pacific Radio Science Conference (URSI AP-RASC)
abstract: Radio wave diagnostics located on board of the spacecraft as well as ground based radio diagnostics can be an excellent tools for diagnostics the local properties of the space plasma as the remote region of space and extra galactic sources. In order to give a more detailed and complete understanding of physical plasma processes that govern the solar terrestrial space, and to develop qualitative and quantitative models of the magnetosphere ionosphere thermosphere coupling, it is necessary to design and build the next generation of construct new types of space plasma multi-point and multi-type sensors and analysis techniques for space diagnostics and monitoring. Novel ground based wide area sensor networks, such as the LOFAR (Low Frequency Array) radar facility, comprising wide band, and vector sensing radio receivers and multi-spacecraft plasma diagnostics should help solve outstanding problems of space physics and describe long-term environmental changes. The main purpose of this presentation is to describe new advanced diagnostic techniques of the near Earth space plasma and point out the scientific challenges of the radio frequency analyser located on board of low orbiting satellites and LOFAR facilities.

articleTitle: Random beamforming combined with receive beamforming in mmWave multiuser MIMO downlink
publicationTitle: 2016 URSI Asia-Pacific Radio Science Conference (URSI AP-RASC)
abstract: The performance of transmit random beamforming (RBF) with receive beamforming at each user is investigated for millimeter wave (mmWave) multiuser multiple-input multiple-output (MU-MIMO) downlink systems. It is shown that RBF in MU-MIMO systems with the total transmit power inversely proportional to the number of receive antennas can achieve the performance of the conventional RBF scheme with the constant total transmit power in MU multiple-input single-output (MISO) systems with no receive beamforming, when the number of transmit antennas is large.

articleTitle: Electromagnetics computational modelling of magnetic metamaterials for wireless power transfe
publicationTitle: 2016 URSI Asia-Pacific Radio Science Conference (URSI AP-RASC)
abstract: We design a compact metamaterial structure enabling the wireless power transfer(WPT) system to enhance its function and model it for electromagnetic characterization. To couple the transmitting and receiving loops of the system compliant with the A4WP requirements, the metamaterial should resonate at a very low frequency as an effectively magnetic device. Additionally, they must be substantially small for the low frequency far below 10 MHz, taking into account the integration to practical handheld devices. The miniaturized structure is simulated through a full-wave method, and its magnetic properties are investigated through the so-called retrieval algorithm to extract its effective permeability. The analysis results present the relationship between the WPT coupling device and metamaterial constitutive parameters.

articleTitle: Analysis of clustered SC-FDMA intermodulation distortion on LTE spectrum
publicationTitle: 2016 URSI Asia-Pacific Radio Science Conference (URSI AP-RASC)
abstract: In wireless communication system, power amplifier is essential in order to increase the signal to be transmitted. However, because of the non-linear system characteristic, the intermodulation distortion signals are generated as well. They can affect the system performance such as minimum sensitivity level and increase a block error rate. In this paper, we focus on a clustered SC-FDMA transmission intermodulation distortion on LTE commercial spectrum and investigate the effect of several-order intermodulation distortion.

articleTitle: Cloud observation using the Ka band cloud radar of CUIT
publicationTitle: 2016 URSI Asia-Pacific Radio Science Conference (URSI AP-RASC)
abstract: This paper will present the performance of Ka-band cloud radar designed by CUIT. Sample observations from this Ka-band solid-state radar for non-precipitation and weak precipitation events during October 2015 and March 2016 will be shown. In addition, the data quality control will be detailed, and the bin-by-bin based attenuation correction methodology using different K-Z relations will be presented.

articleTitle: A matrix form representation of 3-D impedance method for calculations of induced electric fields and currents
publicationTitle: 2016 URSI Asia-Pacific Radio Science Conference (URSI AP-RASC)
abstract: The 3-D impedance method is used to obtain induced electric fields or currents within the biological body caused by magnetic fields in the frequency range for which quasi-static approximation is applied. In this study, the specific structure of matrix for the 3-D impedance method is formulated to use widely used numerical matrix solvers. Consequently, it is confirmed that appropriate solution for the 3-D impedance method is obtained by using the matrix we have formulated in this study.

articleTitle: IPS test observation with DVAC
publicationTitle: 2016 URSI Asia-Pacific Radio Science Conference (URSI AP-RASC)
abstract: The Sun can influence our earth through solar wind, and solar wind is the main source of the interplanetary medium. Therefore, monitoring the Sun and solar wind is of great importance to study the solar-earth phenomenon and to predict the space weather. Ground-based Interplanetary Scintillation (IPS) observation is an efficient and economical way to study the solar wind, and can also exam the shock wave and CME. It has both scientific research and application value. China has begun to observe IPS since 1999 with MSRT, then with some other single dish radio telescopes in China. From 2015, some experimental observations were carried out with the 15m radio telescope DVAC adopting the single station single frequency mode, and some progress has been achieved.

articleTitle: VLBI astrometry up to 130 GHz using multi frequency calibration
publicationTitle: 2016 URSI Asia-Pacific Radio Science Conference (URSI AP-RASC)
abstract: Simultaneous observations at multiple frequency bands have the potential to overcome the fundamental limitation imposed by the atmospheric propagation in mm-VLBI observations. The propagation effects place a severe limit in the sensitivity achievable in mm-VLBI, reducing the time over which the signals can be coherently combined, and preventing the use of phase referencing and astrometric measurements. We carried out simultaneous observations at 22, 43, 87 and 130 GHz of a group of five AGNs, the weakest of which is ca. 200 mJy at 130 GHz, with angular separations ranging from 3.6 to 11 degrees, using the KVN. We analysed this data using the Frequency Phase Transfer (FPT) and the Source Frequency Phase Referencing (SFPR) techniques, which use the observations at a lower frequency to correct those at a higher frequency. The results of the analysis provide an empirical demonstration of the increase in the coherence times at 130 GHz from a few tens of seconds to about twenty minutes, with FPT, and up to many hours with SFPR. Moreover the astrometric analysis provides high precision relative position measurements between two frequencies, including, for the first time, astrometry at 130 GHz.

articleTitle: Basic properties of time-reversal image of target in clutter environment
publicationTitle: 2016 URSI Asia-Pacific Radio Science Conference (URSI AP-RASC)
abstract: This paper provides a feasibility study regarding time-reversal detection scheme of a target inside a clutter environment. An experiment to obtain microwave imaging of target and fixed clutters is performed. For the time-varying environment, a numerical simulation is performed to detect the target based on the self-average characteristics of the time-reversal technique.

articleTitle: The performance analysis for the spatial correlated MIMO systems in V2V
publicationTitle: 2016 URSI Asia-Pacific Radio Science Conference (URSI AP-RASC)
abstract: This paper analyzes the reception performance of the double space-time transmit diversity (DSTTD) with spatial modulation (SM) in vehicle-to-vehicle (V2V) channel. The DSTTD-SM scheme improves the performance of spectral efficiency and reception in V2V environments. The conventional multi-input multi-output (MIMO) schemes are also analyzed in the view of the antenna correlated channel and the spectral efficiency. And the simulation results shows DSTTD-SM scheme has better performance than conventional MIMO schemes in V2V channels which have Rician channel properties with correlation between transmit antennas and Doppler effects.

articleTitle: Polarization simulation for Mingantu Ultrawide SpEctral Radioheliograph
publicationTitle: 2016 URSI Asia-Pacific Radio Science Conference (URSI AP-RASC)
abstract: The MUSER(Mingantu Ultrawide SpEctral Radioheliograph) is a new generation of solar dedicated radio telescope of which the instruments construction has been finished. Its objective is to obtain high quality solar images include dual circular (L, R) polarized signals in wide band. Its ultra-wide band dual-circular polarized feed is one of the key technologies. The polarization performance of the feed is important. So we simulate the polarization performance with CASA and some results are introduced.

articleTitle: Improving the resolution of diagnostics of inhomogeneous plasma media in conditions of strong phase variations
publicationTitle: 2016 URSI Asia-Pacific Radio Science Conference (URSI AP-RASC)
abstract: This report addresses the problem of increasing the resolution of diagnostics of inhomogeneous plasma media with the aid of the spatial field processing obtained from representation of wave field as the double weighted Fourier transform (DWFT) and the single spatial processing of field in the form of Fresnel inversion. We study the effects of spatial discretization of measurements on results of field processing in conditions of strong phase variations. As a model of field scattered by irregularities we use an integral representation in the form of DWFT.

articleTitle: Investigating electromagnetic power transfer ratio of circular polarizing planar metasurface lens
publicationTitle: 2016 URSI Asia-Pacific Radio Science Conference (URSI AP-RASC)
abstract: We designed an antenna structure with the circular polarization metamaterial superstrate which increases the directivity of the primary antenna as a lens. The metamaterial superstrate removes the necessity of the array antenna and complicated feed. Plus, it provides the Fabry-perot cavity with the circular polarization. With regard to the primary antenna, a CRLH antenna is adopted to have the size-reduction from the conventional half-wavelength patch antenna.

articleTitle: Tapered dielectric nanorod antenna at optical wavelengths
publicationTitle: 2016 URSI Asia-Pacific Radio Science Conference (URSI AP-RASC)
abstract: A directive radiation element, tapered dielectric nanorod antenna, fed by a metal-insulator-metal waveguide is studied at optical wavelengths. The characteristics are numerically investigated with the frequency-dependent FDTD method. The tapered nanorod achieves a higher actual gain than that with a nanodipole, with a low reflectivity of 0.07 being retained.

articleTitle: A long baseline airborne SAR interferometry for tidal flat mapping
publicationTitle: 2016 URSI Asia-Pacific Radio Science Conference (URSI AP-RASC)
abstract: Topographic change due to sedimentation and erosion of tidal flat is important for recognizing environmental changes and possible threatens. The tidal flat generally has small topographic variations and high moisture soil surfaces. The conventional SAR interferometric techniques cannot be used for generating DEMs in these tidal flats due to relatively short baseline. In this study, we developed a long-baseline airborne interferometric SAR (InSAR) system that has small ambiguity height and collected airborne InSAR data in the western coast of Korean peninsula. The constructed topographies using the long-baseline airborne InSAR were compared with GPS-RTK measurements.

articleTitle: Evaluation of verification devices with precise probe measurement system in NMIJ
publicationTitle: 2016 URSI Asia-Pacific Radio Science Conference (URSI AP-RASC)
abstract: The paper discusses about evaluation of verification devices in on-wafer measurement. To eliminate effect of probe positioning repeatability, an automatic controlled probing system and a position-adjustment system were established. The established systems can reduce operator-derived probe positional errors. Consequently, the verification devices were evaluated with lower uncertainty owing to the systems. It was found that each of the devices exhibited different errors due to different characteristics of device.

articleTitle: Microwave transversal and recursive-filter based negative group delay circuits and non-Foster elements
publicationTitle: 2016 URSI Asia-Pacific Radio Science Conference (URSI AP-RASC)
abstract: This paper presents some latest developments in microwave transversal and recursive-filter based negative group delay circuits as well as their potential applications in realizing non-Foster elements. By using transversal and recursive-filter approaches, the desired amount of negative group delay can be synthesized with an increased bandwidth. The fully distributed topology of the proposed negative group delay circuits makes it feasible to be further scaled up to higher frequency ranges such as millimeter waves. In addition, it is shown that the proposed transversal-filter based negative group delay circuit is able to create non-Foster elements exhibiting unconditional stability, enabling a new perspective of realizing non-Foster elements.

articleTitle: Joint cell association and resource scheduling for OFDMA multi-cell HetNets
publicationTitle: 2016 URSI Asia-Pacific Radio Science Conference (URSI AP-RASC)
abstract: In this paper, we study a joint cell association and opportunistic resource scheduling scheme for an OFDMA multicell heterogeneous network (HetNet) in an integrated and unified framework. To this end, we formulate the optimization problem and solve it with a dual approach to develop a scheduling scheme.

articleTitle: Diamond devices for RF applications
publicationTitle: 2016 URSI Asia-Pacific Radio Science Conference (URSI AP-RASC)
abstract: Diamond possesses a combination of ecepctional physical properties such as high breakdown field and carrier mobility, and therefore is expected to be high-efficient high-power devices. We solved a carrier doping by using nitrogen dioxide (NO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>). In addition, we greatly improved stability by using aluminum oxide (Al<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>O<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub>) layer.
